name: make
description: Executes build rules from a Makefile: rebuilds only what changed, in the right order, in parallel.

flags.description: Build a specific target: make install, make clean.
-j: parallel build using N jobs (use core count).
Dry run: print commands without executing.

examples.explanation: Builds using every CPU core — the standard invocation for source builds.
Deletes build artifacts (via the clean rule) and rebuilds from scratch.
Shows what install WOULD do before running it — a safety check for unfamiliar Makefiles.

about: A Makefile maps targets to prerequisites and recipes (which MUST be indented with tabs, not spaces — the classic make error). make compares file timestamps: changed sources trigger recompilation of only what depends on them. Most open-source builds follow the ./configure && make && sudo make install pattern.
useCases: Automating repetitive task chains (test, build, deploy).
mistakes: Indenting recipes with spaces — make requires TABs; "*** missing separator" is the telltale error.
Running make install from untrusted source without checking -n first.
warnings: sudo make install places files system-wide (/usr/local); prefer package managers or check with -n what it will do.
